title: U.S. House · Texas's 4th District
area: Northeast Texas, including part of Collin County and areas toward the Oklahoma and Arkansas borders

context.text: Incumbent Pat Fallon (R) defeated Don Horn in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Jason Pearce defeated Andrew Rubell in the Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Pat Fallon

summary.text: Pat Fallon is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 4th Congressional District, a former Frisco city council member and Texas legislator.

background.text: Born in Pittsfield, Massachusetts, in 1967; earned a degree in government and international relations from the University of Notre Dame in 1990.
Served as an active-duty U.S. Air Force officer for four years, receiving an honorable discharge at the rank of captain; later worked as an entrepreneur and as president and CEO of Virtus Apparel.
Served on the Frisco city council (2009–2012), in the Texas House of Representatives (2013–2019), and in the Texas Senate (2019–2021) before being elected to Congress.

record.text: Serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (including the Delivering on Government Efficiency Subcommittee) and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence in the 2025–2026 Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey or curated key-messages profile was found for Fallon in this race's coverage; positions on specific issues were not documented from the sources checked.

candidates.name: Jason Pearce
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Jason Pearce is a first-time candidate running as the Democratic nominee for Texas's 4th Congressional District on a message of reducing the influence of money in politics.

background.text: Born and raised in Plano, Texas, in 1993; describes his background as working multiple jobs and long hours before running for office.

priorities.text: Supports term limits and mandatory retirement at age 65 for all offices, including the judiciary.
Supports banning lobbying by former members of Congress and overturning Citizens United v. FEC to reduce the role of PAC money in politics.
